requirements.text: Posting an object with the Flask test client's json parameter marks the request as JSON, request.get_json() returns the same object, and returning it produces an HTTP 200 application/json response with the same data.
A request body containing the JSON string alpha with content type application/x+json is recognized as JSON and request.get_json() returns alpha.
A malformed body sent with content type application/json causes request.get_json() to produce HTTP 400 instead of executing a successful JSON response.
Calling jsonify with no positional or keyword arguments returns an application/json response whose JSON value is null.
Calling jsonify with multiple positional values returns an application/json array that preserves positional order and values.
Calling jsonify with keyword arguments returns an application/json object; the default provider sorts keys and emits compact output outside debug mode.
The default JSON provider escapes non-ASCII characters when ensure_ascii is true and emits the literal Unicode character when ensure_ascii is false.
Calling jsonify with both positional and keyword arguments raises TypeError with the message app.json.response() takes either args or kwargs, not both.

test_cases.title: JSON client object round-trips through the request and response
preconditions: An isolated Flask app exposes a POST route that returns request.get_json().

steps.action: POST the object using the test client's json parameter.
steps.expected_result: HTTP 200; request.is_json is true; parsed request and JSON response equal the supplied object; response mimetype is application/json.

test_cases.expected_outcome: A normal JSON object round-trips without data loss.

test_cases.title: Structured-suffix JSON mimetype is accepted
preconditions: An isolated POST route passes request.get_json() to jsonify so the parsed scalar is observable as a JSON response.

steps.action: POST the JSON string with application/x+json.
steps.expected_result: HTTP 200 and response JSON value alpha.

test_cases.expected_outcome: The structured-suffix JSON mimetype is parsed as JSON.

test_cases.title: Malformed JSON is rejected
preconditions: An isolated POST route calls request.get_json().

steps.expected_result: HTTP 400 and the successful route response is not returned.

test_cases.expected_outcome: Malformed JSON cannot pass the request parser.

test_cases.title: jsonify without arguments returns JSON null
preconditions: An isolated GET route returns jsonify().

steps.expected_result: HTTP 200, application/json, parsed value null, raw body null followed by newline.

test_cases.expected_outcome: The empty argument boundary maps to JSON null.

test_cases.title: Multiple jsonify positional values preserve list order
preconditions: An isolated GET route returns jsonify('alpha', 2, false).

steps.expected_result: HTTP 200, application/json, parsed array [alpha, 2, false] in that order.

test_cases.expected_outcome: Multiple positional values become one ordered JSON array.

test_cases.title: Keyword jsonify output is sorted and compact
preconditions: The default provider runs outside debug mode.

steps.action: GET a route returning jsonify(status='ok', count=2).
steps.expected_result: HTTP 200 and exact body {"count":2,"status":"ok"} followed by newline.

test_cases.expected_outcome: Default keyword serialization is a sorted compact JSON object.

test_cases.title: ensure_ascii controls Unicode escaping
preconditions: An isolated GET route jsonify-serializes a snowman character.

steps.action: Request with ensure_ascii=true, then with ensure_ascii=false.
steps.expected_result: The first body contains the escape \u2603; the second contains the literal UTF-8 snowman; both parse to the same character.

test_cases.expected_outcome: Unicode representation follows the configured provider flag without changing the logical value.

test_cases.title: jsonify rejects mixed positional and keyword arguments

steps.action: Call jsonify with both argument forms.
steps.expected_result: TypeError is raised with exact contract message app.json.response() takes either args or kwargs, not both.

test_cases.expected_outcome: Ambiguous JSON response construction is rejected before response creation.

warnings: Bounded feature — cases cover eight source-backed JSON request/response contracts only.
Project integrity — no test may require changing Flask source, existing tests or dependency state.
